prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; restrictive degraded-platform states; explicit controller restoration of automatic departure. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern), non-vital: sends Crew Login Token Bundle; previews actions; displays positions/alarms/faults, excludes maintenance commands. Line Traffic Controller: regulation, Temporary Speed Restriction Notice, incident/recovery decisions; receives Route Release Exception List from West Junction Interlocking. Dispatch requires confirmation/cancellation; station holds never replace locking. Voice Dispatch Console identifies caller/platform/hold; Revenue Train Operator reads back/reports hazards/cab/handling/passenger impacts; voice cannot replace safety validation. North District Zone Controller (Marble)/South District Zone Controller (Orchid): district/turnback/approach control; transfers require ownership/overlap/receiver-validation; restrictive evidence governs. Both log health/interfaces/fallback/boundary events. East Junction Interlocking (Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking: proved points/overlaps/flanks before authority; checked detection/correspondence/opposing routes before release; log commands/detection/locks. East sends Axle Counter Reset Request; forbidden during route/approach locking. Axle counters independently prove availability; Maple (unidentified) records clearance. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot; not route-proof; compatible doors/berth constrain departure. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token, rejects stale acknowledgements; enforces profiles; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; stores faults/authority-acceptance/propulsion-cutback/interface-exceptions. Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed/confidence/plausibility; disagreement increases uncertainty/separation, retained diagnostically. Train Radio Modem uses Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron), sends Radio Handover Audit File; degradation retains validated authority; logs loss/reconnection/quality/retries. Saffron/Safety Data Communication Network provide performance records; latter separates safety/nonvital traffic. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance checks certificates/clocks, produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack in approved-maintenance, used before renewed sessions. Service Timetable Server supplies approved/controller-verified context; Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled context. Safety parts timestamp changes/accepted/rejected commands/loss/protection. Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives monitored fixed/onboard events without authority alteration; compares checksum identifiers/baseline. Signal Maintenance

New part:
S167: Failure triage first establishes whether the condition is safety critical, service affecting, cyber security related, or a maintenance-only defect.
S168: Safety critical failures remain under traffic control coordination until the Line Traffic Controller confirms the operating restriction and a Signal Maintenance Engineer confirms the engineering status.
S169: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server preserves raw events, normalised event records, diagnostic session notes, and file integrity values for post-incident analysis.
S170: Configuration records include software build identifiers, parameter set identifiers, radio configuration versions, interlocking data versions, and approved change references.
S171: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance maintains certificate and key status records used to verify whether communications faults could be related to authentication or expiry conditions.
S172: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway are checked when reported symptoms involve timetable-driven routing assumptions or passenger-facing messages rather than train control protection.
S173: The Voice Dispatch Console is included in the evidence scope when verbal instructions, emergency calls, or manual coordination affected the response to an event.
S174: After a reportable incident, retained evidence is frozen under maintenance control, copied to a protected repository, and released only through the agreed engineering investigation process.
S175: During degraded operation, Greenvale Metro keeps trains stationary or moving at controlled speed until separation assurance is restored.
S176: A degraded mode is declared by the Line Traffic Controller when automatic movement authority, train localization, point detection, platform interface, or radio continuity cannot be trusted.
S177: The Metro Operations Control System shall present the affected limits, the selected fallback mode, and any pending operator actions without obscuring safety alarms.
S178: The Atlas Onboard Controller transitions to restricted manual operation when valid movement authority is unavailable or when onboard location confidence falls below the configured threshold.
S179: The Revenue Train Operator remains responsible for speed control, stopping accuracy, door release discipline, and compliance with verbal movement limits during restricted manual operation.
S180: The Dual Channel Odometer shall cause the train location to be treated as uncertain when its channels disagree beyond the permitted tolerance.
S181: The Train Radio Modem shall report loss of safe data connectivity to the Atlas Onboard Controller and shall not mask intermittent communication failures from the cab display.
S182: A failure in the Wayside Radio Access Network is handled by reducing train throughput before any extension of manual working is considered.
S183: The North District Zone Controller applies the Temporary Speed Restriction Notice only after validating the affected track limits against its degraded-mode map.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
